newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales active $63 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sales active $63 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle Tuesday sold at $63.00 per cwt in active trading following a slow start near midday, feedlot sources said. The sales were steady with last week.
About 35,000 head sold in Kansas and another estimated 35,000 in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
Cattle had been priced at $64.00 but traded at $63.00 as feedlots attempted to remain current going into an expected increase in supplies the next four to five weeks, several feedlot sources said.
Packers reportedly were in the market early this week so they could line up live cattle inventories for plant startups following the three-day holiday weekend, the sources said.
Cattle rates of gain were not adversely affected by hot weather in the Plains this week because temperatures and humidity went down at night, they said.

Daytime high temperatures Tuesday were in the upper 90s Fahrenheit from central Nebraska through Kansas and in the low 100s in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma, the feedlot sources said. However, evening temperatures dipped to the low-to-mid 60s, they said.
"Cool nights in the summertime can be a real advantage for cattle performance," one Panhandle feedlot source said.
